name: WebGL2 paints where WebGPU does not, and the strip painters keep their parts
summary: A page with no real WebGPU adapter paints with Vello GPU on a hardware WebGL2 context before it falls back to the CPU, and both strip painters keep their settled parts, so a frame no longer rebuilds and cuts every path.

changes.subject: vKEsyHFk#290spzv7
changes.value: It does what the SVG's stylesheet did: the colours of a theme, the recede of a lit set, the far view and the order in which a selected part is raised. A glyph is drawn from the outlines of the core's own faces. Vello on WebGPU and Vello GPU on WebGL2 implement the same Canvas trait in the browser crate.

changes.subject: vKEsyHFk#hKrzJUPf
changes.value: Chooses the painter of a canvas once, from what the browser says: Vello on WebGPU with a real adapter, Vello GPU on WebGL2 with a hardware context, Vello on the CPU otherwise

changes.subject: vKEsyHFk#hKrzJUPf
changes.value: A software WebGPU adapter, or none, sends the canvas to WebGL2. WebGL2 refuses a context with a major performance caveat and a renderer whose name says it draws in software, and the rule reads no frame back. A WebGPU painter that fails at work gets one more try, and a second failure soon after sends the canvas to WebGL2. A WebGL2 painter that fails or loses its context gives way to the CPU painter. Each new painter takes a fresh canvas, because a canvas that held a GPU context never takes a 2D one. The caller shows which painter draws, and why WebGPU and WebGL2 do not.

changes.subject: vKEsyHFk#irHUnOY7
changes.value: start the WebGPU, WebGL2 or CPU painter

changes.subject: vKEsyHFk#9FxduWoO
changes.value: Until the painter's first frame the surface shows the SVG with its ink, and a painter that cannot start leaves it so: a correct picture. The SVG stays in the page under the canvas as the hidden semantic layer that search, copy, screen readers and the marks read, written by picture-transition.ts. picture-ink.ts keeps a first picture's ink back for a moment so that the painter brings the picture in. React gives the stage a host, and the stage makes each canvas inside it, so a painter that fails is released and a replacement gets a fresh canvas. picture-ink.ts then gives the SVG back the glyphs and definitions that a painted surface dropped, so complete ink shows while the replacement starts. The surface says which painter draws in data-painter, and why WebGPU and WebGL2 do not in data-painter-reason.

changes.subject: vKEsyHFk/vKEsyHFk#OHywsFXm
changes.value: The TypeScript hosts in this package load the renderer core, which crates/ builds to WebAssembly (ADR 0059). The core measures, lays out and paints. A host runs its layout solves and gives it icons and theme colours. A page paints a picture on a canvas with Vello, on WebGPU, on WebGL2 or on the CPU, from the same scene. The SVG stays the product of exports, PNGs and README assets, and stays in the page as the semantic layer. Recordings paint on the CPU.

changes.subject: vKEsyHFk#NFwqWgrm
changes.value: One Canvas trait serves Vello on WebGPU, Vello GPU on WebGL2 and Vello on the CPU, so all three run the same walk over the scene (ADR 0071, ADR 0074). The WebGPU canvas keeps a settled part as an encoded scene. The keeper of the parts module keeps one for both strip canvases as its drawing calls with each stroke's outline, and a frame draws only the kept shapes it can see. The in-between of two scenes is a pure function of the scenes and a progress value, so Rust tests own it. A host tells the stage what changed and what time it is, and asks for frames.

changes.subject: vKEsyHFk#UpjzNLKH
changes.value: The Painter class that a page holds: one stage and the canvas its frames land on, painted by Vello on WebGPU, by Vello GPU on WebGL2 or by Vello on the CPU
